English Literature.question: ১) Which one is the first Tragedy of English literature?
English Literature.exp:
Gorboduc is the first English tragedy written by Norton and Sackville.
The Virtue Rewarded or Pamela is the first English novel. The Spanish Tragedy written by Thomas Kyd and Doctor Faustus written by Christopher Marlowe.
An ABC of English Literature, Dr M Mofizar Rahman.

English Literature.question: ২) Who wrote the first Tragedy of English literature?
English Literature.exp:
Gorboduc, A Play by Thomas Norton and Thomas Sackville takes as its subject Gorboduc, a mythical king of ancient Britain. First performed in 1561, it is the earliest English tragic play in blank verse.
Source: https://www.britannica.com/topic/Gorboduc-by-Norton-and-Sackville

English Literature.question: ৩) Who is known as ''Bird of Avon''?
English Literature.exp:
None is called the Bird of Avon.
The greatest English dramatist, William Shakespeare is often called the ‘Bard of Avon’. He wrote 37 plays and 154 sonnets.
Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

English Literature.question: ৪) ‘Shylock’ is a famous character of -
English Literature.exp: Important character of The merchant of Venice: Antonio, Shylock, Portia etc.

English Literature.question: ৫) Which is the period of ''original romanticism''?
English Literature.exp:
Elizabethan Age (1558 – 1603):
Features:
- ইংল্যান্ডের রাণী Queen Elizabeth এর নামানুসারে নামকরণ।
- এটি Golden Age হিসাবে পরিচিত।
- This period is a period of original romanticism.
- This period was replete with lyrics and songs.
- The literature shows a quest for ‘The remote, the wonderful and beautiful’.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

English Literature.question: ৬) Whose real name was 'Samuel Langhorn Clemens'?
English Literature.exp:
Mark Twain (1835 – 1910):
His real name is Samuel Langhorn Clemens.
Famous Works: The Adventure of Tom Sawyer, The Adventure of Huckleberry Finn.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman and Britannica.

English Literature.question: ৭) Who is the author of ''Antony and Cleopatra''?
English Literature.exp:
William Shakespeare was an English dramatist and poet of the sixteenth century. He is known mostly for his plays. His famous Tragedies are Hamlet, Macbeth, Othello, King Lear, Julius Caesar, Romeo and Juliet, Antony and Cleopatra, Titus Andronicus, Timon of Athens.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

English Literature.question: ৮) Which one is known as Shakespeare's swan song?
English Literature.exp:
Swan song means the final performance or activity of a person's career.
William Shakespeare এর শেষ নাটক Tempest. এটিকে Shakespeare এর Swan song বলা হয়।

English Literature.question: ৯) ‘The Unfortunate Traveller’ was written by -
English Literature.exp:
Thomas Nashe:
- A University Wit.
- Wrote – The Unfortunate Traveller.

Source: Britannica.com

English Literature.question: ১০) Who wrote the play ‘A Tale of Tub’?
English Literature.exp:
‘A Tale of a Tub’ is a well known allegorical satire by Jonathan Swift. But, Ben Johnson also wrote a play by the same name.

Ben Johnson's notable works:
- Volpone
- The Alchemist
- A Tale of Tub
- Every MAn in His Humour
- Every Man out of His Humour
- The Silent Women
- The Devil is an Ass etc.
He is mostly known for his 'Comedy of Humour' which is related to Medical Theory.
Source: Britannica.com

English Literature.question: ১১) ‘Timon of Athens’ written by William Shakespeare is a/an -
English Literature.exp:
Timon of Athens, tragedy in five acts by William Shakespeare, probably written sometime in 1605–08 and published in the First Folio of 1623 from an authorial manuscript, probably unfinished.
Some parts of the play may be by Thomas Middleton. It belongs to Shakespeare’s late experimental period, when he explored a new kind of tragic form.
Shakespeares' other Tragedies are:
Hamlet, Macbeth, Othello, King Lear, Julius Caesar, Romeo and Juliet, Antony and Cleopatra, Titus Andronicus, etc.
Source: Britannica.com

English Literature.question: ১২) Who isn’t a Cavalier Poet?
English Literature.exp: Cavalier Poets are Thomas Carew, John Suckling, Richard Lovelace, Edmund Waller and Robert Herrick.

English Literature.question: ১৩) The age of 'The Romantic Period' is _______.
English Literature.exp:
Neoclassical period (1660-1798)
Restoration Age (1660-1700)
Augustan Period/The Age of Pope (1700-1745)
Age of Sensibility (1745-1785/98)
The Romantic Period (1798-1832)
The Victorian Period (1832-1901)

English Literature.question: ১৪) So farewell Hope, and with Hope farewell ____.
English Literature.exp:
So farewell Hope, and with Hope farewell Fear,
Farewell Remorse: all Good to me is lost;
Evil be thou my Good.
John Milton: Paradise Lost
Source: Britannica

English Literature.question:
১৫) “I’ll love you, dear, I’ll love you
Till China and Africa meet,
And the river jumps over the mountain
And the salmon sing in the street” - is an example of -
English Literature.exp:
Hyperbole is an exaggerated statement or an extreme overstatement.
Example of hyperbole:
“Ten thousand saw I at a glance”
I’ll love you, dear, I’ll love you/Till China and Africa meet,/And the river jumps over the mountain/And the salmon sing in the street- W.H. Auden
It used to create strong emotional responses.
Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

English Literature.question: ১৬) ‘The Conquest of Granada’ is written by -
English Literature.exp:
John Dryden is the Father of Modern English Criticism.
His famous works are- All for Love, The Indian Emperor, Aureng-Zebe, The Mistaken Husband, Absalom and Achitophel, MacFlecknoe, The essay of Dramatic Poesy, The Conquest of Granada, The Medal of John Bays.
[Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman and Live MCQ lecture.]

English Literature.question: ১৭) The character ‘Robinson Crusoe’ is found in which writer’s writing?
English Literature.exp:
‘Robinson Crusoe’, novel by Daniel Defoe, first published in London in 1719. Defoe’s first long work of fiction, it introduced two of the most-enduring characters in English literature: Robinson Crusoe and Friday.
Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica

English Literature.question: ১৮) ‘The Rape of the Lock’ is a/an -
English Literature.exp:
The Rape of the Lock, mock-epic poem in heroic couplets by Alexander Pope. The first version, published in 1712, consisted of two cantos; the final version, published in 1714, was expanded to five cantos. Based on an actual incident and written to reconcile the families that had been estranged by it, The Rape of the Lock recounts the story of a young woman named Belinda who has a lock of hair stolen by an ardent young man.
Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica.

English Literature.question: ১৯) Which one is considered to be the first novel in English Literature?
English Literature.exp:
''Pamela'', in full Pamela; or, ''Virtue Rewarded'', novel in epistolary style by Samuel Richardson, published in 1740 and based on a story about a servant and the man who, failing to seduce her, marries her.
Pamela is often credited with being the first English novel. Although the validity of this claim depends on the definition of the term novel, Richardson was clearly innovative in his concentration on a single action.
Source: Brittanica.com

English Literature.question: ২০) 'Protagonist' indicates -
English Literature.option2: the leading character or actor in a play
English Literature.exp:
Protagonist (noun) the leading character or one of the major characters in a play, film, novel, etc.
Source: Oxford Dictionary.

English Literature.question: ২১) “The Wild Swans at Coole” is a poem written by -
English Literature.exp:
William Butler Yeats (1865 – 1939):
- Irish dramatist, poet and critic.
- He is famous for his use of “Symbolism and Mysticism”.
- He wrote the preamble of Tagore's “Gitanjali” in 1912, which later got nobel prize in 1913.
- W.B Yeats got nobel prize in 1923.
- Major Works:
Poems: The wild swans at coole, The Tower, The Winding Stair and Other poems, The Resurrection, The Second Coming, The Cat and the Moon, Byzantium, The Lake Isle of Innisfree, Among School Children, The Lord of Harts, falling of leaves, A prayer for My Daughter, When You Are Old.
Drama: The countess Cathleen, Cathleen in Houlihan.
Source: Brittanica.com and Live MCQ Lecture

English Literature.question: ২২) Who is the writer of 'Areopagitica'?
English Literature.exp:
John Milton is a writer of Caroline Age. He is called Epic Poet and also called 'A great master of verse in Puritan Period'. His famous Epics are Paradise Lost and Paradise Regained and his famous books are Comus, Lycidas, Of Education and Areopagitica.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman and Live MCQ lecture.

English Literature.question: ২৩) The characters 'Pip, Estella' are created by Charles Dickens found in -
English Literature.exp:
Great Expectations is the famous novel of Charles Dickens.
The important character of this novel is Pip, Estella, Miss Havisham, etc.
Source: Britannica.com.

English Literature.question: ২৪) ‘Lyrical Ballads’ is a collection of romantic poems by-
English Literature.option1: William Wordsworth and P. B. Shelley
English Literature.exp:
The Romantic period began in 1798 with the publication of “Lyrical Ballads” is a collection of romantic poems by William Wordsworth and S.T. Coleridge. Revival of Romanticism took place in the Romantic Period.
Source: Live MCQ Lecture and An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman.

English Literature.question: ২৫) ‘The Rime of the Ancient Mariner’ is a -
English Literature.exp:
‘The Rime of the Ancient Mariner’, poem in seven parts by Samuel Taylor Coleridge that first appeared in Lyrical Ballads, published collaboratively by Coleridge and William Wordsworth in 1798.
[Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ২৬) Shakespeare composed much of his plays in what sort of verse?
English Literature.exp: Shakespeare composed much of his plays in Iambic pentameter sort of verse. Here “Iambic pentameter” means a line of verse with five metrical feet, each consisting of one short (or unstressed) syllable followed by one long (or stressed) syllable.

English Literature.question: ২৭) Anti-romantic novelist of the Romantic age-
English Literature.exp:
Jane Austen (1775 – 1817):
Novelist.
She is called an anti-romantic novelist in the Romantic age because of her stern attitude against youthful passion.
Source: Live MCQ Lecture.

English Literature.question: ২৮) The pen name of ‘Henry Fielding’ is -
English Literature.exp:
Henry Fielding is regarded as the 'Father of Modern English Novel'.
He is famous for Picaresque Novels.
His pen name is Captain Hercules Vinegar.
His famous plays are: Rape Upon Rape, The Temple Beau, The Tragedy of Tragedies, The Modern Husband and his famous Novels are Tom Jones, Amelia, Joseph Andrews.
[Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman and Live MCQ Lecture]

English Literature.question: ২৯) 'Ode to the West Wind' is written by ___.
English Literature.exp:
Percy Bysshe Shelley (1792 – 1822):
This English poet was an atheist and expelled from Oxford University in 1811 due to his publication of a pamphlet named “The necessity of Atheism”.
He believed that only revolution can change our society. So that he is called “Revolutionary Poet”.
He is also called “The poet of Hope and Regeneration”.
Shelly mourns over the death of John Keats in his famous elegy “Adonais”.
Major works: Prometheus Unbound (1820), Adonais (1821), A Defense of poetry (1820), Ode to the West Wind, To a skylark, The Revolt of Islam, Alastor, Ozymandias, Queen Mab, The cloud.
Source: Live MCQ Lecture

English Literature.question: ৩০) ‘Ode a Grecian Urn’ is written by -
English Literature.exp:
Heard melodies are sweet, but those unheard are sweeter.
-Ode a Grecian Urn
-John Keats
Source: Live MCQ Lecture

English Literature.question: ৩১) Charles Robert Darwin is the author of -
English Literature.exp:
Charles Robert Darwin (1809-82) is a writer of The Victorian Period. His major works are:
The Origin of Species (1859)
The Descent of Man (1871)
Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr. M Mofizar Rahman

English Literature.question: ৩২) Who is the poet of the 'Victorian Age'?
English Literature.exp:
The most prolific and well-regarded poets of the 'Victorian Age' included Lord Tennyson, Robert Browning, Elizabeth Barrett Browning, Matthew Arnold, Gerard Manley Hopkins, and Oscar Wilde.
Source: britannica.com

English Literature.question: ৩৩) ''It was the best of times, it was the worst of times, it was the age of wisdom, it was the age of foolishness, it was the epoch of belief, it was the epoch of incredulity.'' quoted by-
English Literature.exp:
This is the first line of the novel A Tale of Two Cities. It is a historical novel by Charles Dickens, set in London and Paris before and during the French Revolution.
Famous quotations of Charles Dickens are-
''It was the best of times, it was the worst of times, it was the age of wisdom, it was the age of foolishness, it was the epoch of belief, it was the epoch of incredulity, it was the season of light, it was the season of darkness, it was the spring of hope, it was the winter of despair.'' (A Tale of Two Cities).
''There is a passion for hunting something deeply implanted in the human breast.''
''It is far, it is far better thing that I do, than I have ever done; it is far, it is a far, far better rest that I go to then I have ever known.
Source: Live MCQ Lecture.

English Literature.question: ৩৪) Who wrote the novel “Vanity Fair”?
English Literature.exp:
Vanity Fair, novel of early 19th-century English society by William Makepeace Thackeray, published serially in monthly installments from 1847 to 1848 and in book form in 1848. Thackeray’s previous writings had been published either unsigned or under pseudonyms; Vanity Fair was the first work he published under his own name. It is subtitled A Novel Without a Hero, Vanity Fair metaphorically represents the human condition.
Source: britannica.com

English Literature.question: ৩৫) Whose real name is Mary Ann Evans -
English Literature.exp:
Mary Ann Evans is the original name of George Eliot.
Famous literary works of George Eliot -
The Mill on the Floss, Scenes of Clerical Life, Adam Bede, Silas Marner, Romola, Middlemarch.
Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr. M Mofizar Rahman

English Literature.question: ৩৬) ‘The Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam’ is translated by -
English Literature.exp:
Edward Fitzgerald (1809-83): The Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam (1859), translated into English from Persian.
Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr. M Mofizar Rahman

English Literature.question: ৩৭) “Man and Superman” is -
English Literature.exp:
Man and Superman - is a satirical comedy in genre.
It is a four acts play by George Bernard Shaw, published in 1903 and performed (without scene 2 of Act III) in 1905; the first complete performance was in 1915.
His notable works are -
“Pygmalion”
“Mrs. Warren’s Profession”
“Arms and the Man”
“Saint Joan”
“Heartbreak House”
“Major Barbara”
“Caesar and Cleopatra”
“Man and Superman”
“The Doctor’s Dilemma”
“Androcles and the Lion”
Source: Britannica.com

English Literature.question: ৩৮) 'Death in the Afternoon' is written by -
English Literature.exp:
Ernest Hemingway is an American novelist. He was awarded the Nobel prize in 1954 for literature.
Death in the Afternoon is a novel written by Ernest Hemingway, which was published in 1932.
His other famous novels are-
- The Old Man and The Sea,
- A Farewell to Arms,
- The Sun Also Rises,
- For Whom the Bell Tolls,
- To Have and Have not etc.
Source: Britannica.com

English Literature.question: ৩৯) Who won the Nobel prize in literature for 'Lord of the Flies'?
English Literature.exp:
ব্রিটিশ ঔপন্যাসিক, নাট্যকার ও কবি William Gerald Golding তার Lord of the Files উপন্যাসের জন্যে ১৯৮৩ সালে সাহিত্যে নোবেল পুরস্কার লাভ করেন।
তার অন্যান্য উপন্যাসের মধ্যে The Scorpion God Free Fall, The Pyramid, Darkness Visible উল্লেখযোগ্য।
সূত্রঃ লাইভ এমসিকিউ লেকচার।

English Literature.question: ৪০) ‘September on Jessore Road’ is written by -
English Literature.exp:
September on Jessore Road is a poem by Allen Ginsberg on refugees from Bangladesh Liberation war in 1971. During Bangladesh's Liberation War in 1971, the US government was an ally of Pakistan and even sent its 7th fleet to intimidate India from interfering with the events in then East Pakistan.
Source: The New York Times.

English Literature.question: ৪১) 'India Wins Freedom' is written by -
English Literature.exp:
India Wins Freedom বইটি ভারতীয় জাতীয় কংগ্রেস নেতা মাওলানা আবুল কালাম আজাদ রচিত আত্মজীবনীমূলক গ্রন্থ। এটি ১৯৮৮ সালে প্রকাশিত হয়। আবুল কালাম আজাদ কংগ্রেসের সাবেক সভাপতি এবং ভারতের প্রথম শিক্ষামন্ত্রী ছিলেন।
সূত্রঃ বাংলাপিডিয়া।

English Literature.question: ৪২) 1984 and Animal Farm, these two novels are written by -
English Literature.exp:
George Orwell এর আসল নাম হলো Eric Arthur Blair. তিনি ব্রিটিশ ভারতে জন্মগ্রহণ করেন। Animal Farm এবং Nineteen Eighty Four জর্জ অরওয়েলের দুটি বিখ্যাত উপন্যাস।
Works:
Novel:
Animal Farm (1945 – a fairy story)
Nineteen Eighty-Four
Burmese Days
Coming up for Air.
Story/Essay: Shooting an Elephant, A Hanging.
Source: Live MCQ Lecture and Encyclopedia Britannica.

English Literature.question: ৪৩) Who is the Writer of 'Modern Period'?
English Literature.exp:
Lord Byron and William Hazlitt are the poets of the Romantic Period. Albert Camus is the modern poet.
Source: Live MCQ lecture.

English Literature.question: ৪৪) ‘The Metamorphosis’ is a Novella by -
English Literature.exp: The Metamorphosis, symbolic story by Austrian writer Franz Kafka, published in German as Die Verwandlung in 1915.

English Literature.question: ৪৫) Which is a famous allegory in prose?
English Literature.exp:
The Pilgrim's Progress, the famous allegory in prose, is written by John Bunyan.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

English Literature.question: ৪৬) Which years can be called the Elizabethan period in English Literature?
English Literature.exp:
The Elizabethan Period is called 'the Golden age of English literature'.
Duration of Elizabethan Period is 1558 to 1603. The other titles of this age: Glorious Period of English literature, Golden Period of English Drama, A nest of singing birds.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman and Live MCQ Lecture.

English Literature.question: ৪৭) Who of the following is a University Wit?
English Literature.exp:
Elizabethan Period এর একদল Young dramatist and pamphleteers (ক্ষুদ্র পুস্তিকা রচয়িতা) দেরকে University Wits বলা হয়।
তাঁরা Oxford and Cambridge University এর Scholar/Witty students ছিলেন। তাঁরা অনেক বিখ্যাত নাটক রচনা ও মঞ্চস্থ করার মাধ্যমে খ্যাতি অর্জন করেছিলেন। University Wits ছিলেন মোট ৭ জন।
এঁরা হলেন- Christopher Marlowe, Thomas Kyd, Robert Greene, George Peele, Thomas Nashe, John Lyly and Thomas Lodge.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

English Literature.question: ৪৮) Who wrote ‘Utopia’?
English Literature.exp:
The word first occurred in Sir Thomas More’s Utopia, published in Latin as Libellus…de optimo reipublicae statu, deque nova insula Utopia (1516; “Concerning the highest state of the republic and the new island Utopia”); it was compounded by More from the Greek words for “not” (ou) and “place” (topos) and thus meant “nowhere.”
[ Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ৪৯) Who wrote “Ralph Roister Doister”?
English Literature.exp:
Nicholas Udall wrote the first known English comedy, Ralph Roister Doister. In 1553.
Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

English Literature.question: ৫০) Which one is not a type of sonnet?
English Literature.exp:
A poem of fourteen iambic pentameter lines is called a sonnet. It is of three types: Petrarchan, Shakespearean, Spenserian.
Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman
